Puerto Nariño · Colombian Amazon

Daytime kayaking in the Amazon

Slow down on the water. A daylight kayaking experience, shaped by the river.

Ask Amaru on WhatsApp ↗

About this experience

Kaya is our daytime paddling experience in the Amazon. Follow the water at a slower pace and take in the forest surroundings by natural light. It is a separate outing from the rainforest night walk; the route, equipment and suitability for your group need to be discussed before choosing it.

Water is part of everyday travel around Puerto Nariño. Paddling offers a closer perspective on the river landscape: the line of the bank, the shade of trees and the changing reflections. Kaya is Amaru’s daytime experience, with natural light for taking in the surroundings and time to enjoy the simple rhythm of moving across the water.

The Amazon’s waterways change with water levels and weather. Those changes are part of planning a paddling outing, so choose your experience by discussing the conditions for your visit. If you are drawn to quiet scenery, photography or trying paddling for the first time, share that interest so Amaru can explain the options and requirements.

Destination context sources: Colombia Travel ↗

What to explore

  • Daylight outings only
  • Route adapted to water levels and weather
  • Equipment and requirements confirmed in your proposal

Before you go

Time of day
DAYTIME
Duration
Confirm the duration and meeting point with Amaru for your dates.

Choose clothes that can get wet and protect electronics in a waterproof bag. Bring sun protection and drinking water. Tell Amaru about your paddling experience and ask about the craft, life jacket, guiding arrangements, current and requirements for your group. Suitability for beginners or children needs confirmation before choosing the outing.

What should I confirm?

Ask about the route, departure, group requirements, guide language, equipment, transport and what is included. Share your dates and number of travellers, and review the full price and cancellation conditions before confirming anything.

Routes depend on water levels, weather and local conditions. Wildlife sightings cannot be guaranteed.
